MD11F.description: A pilot's aircraft. The MD-11F carries a big load a long way and is a favourite on medical and humanitarian long-haul flights. It has a high approach speed and a small horizontal tail, which make it demanding to land. A smooth MD-11 touchdown is something PAC crews take pride in.

B77F.description: The longest-legged aircraft in the fleet. The 777F flies nonstop sectors that other freighters need a fuel stop for, on two engines and at a much lower cost per pound than a four-engine jet. It runs the long intercontinental lanes: Hong Kong to Milan, Johannesburg to Frankfurt, and the transpacific rotations through Anchorage.

A306F.description: The A300-600F gives PAC widebody volume on regional and medium-haul lanes. Its wide main deck takes standard containers side by side, so it carries roughly twice what a 737 can on trunk routes like Cincinnati to the West Coast or Milan to the Mediterranean, while still working from mid-size airports.

B738F.description: Converted from passenger 737-800s with a large forward side cargo door and a reinforced main deck, the 737-800BCF/BDSF is the backbone of PAC's short and medium-haul express flying. It is cheap to operate, fits almost any airport, and turns fast on overnight parcel runs and island resupply.

R722F.description: The 727-200F re-engined by Valsan: the two outer engines are swapped for quieter, more powerful JT8D-217s, the same engine as the MD-80, and the cockpit is upgraded to a more modern glass layout in place of the original analog gauges. That gives better takeoff and climb performance, a lower noise footprint and a more modern flight deck than the classic 727 freighter. The center engine is unchanged, the main deck is the same, and it’s a bit more capable on short and hot runways.
R722F.name: Boeing 727-200F Super 27

B722F.description: The classic 727 freighter: three P&W JT8D-9 engines, a fully analog flight deck and a three-person crew with a flight engineer. It needs more runway and more hands-on flying than the re-engined Super 27, but it’s the original 727 experience.
B722F.engines: 3 × P&W JT8D-9 (the FSS 200F uses the -9 engine)
B722F.name: Boeing 727-200F

B763F.description: Widebody volume at twin-engine cost. The 767-300F carries more than the A300 over longer sectors, which makes it ideal for transcontinental express flying, Latin America lanes out of Miami and the busier Europe to Middle East routes.

B752F.description: The overnight express workhorse. The 757-200F has a huge amount of thrust for its size, so it climbs out of short runways fully loaded and cruises fast on medium-haul sectors. It's the aircraft of choice for domestic trunk routes out of Cincinnati and Caribbean relief flights.

B742F.description: The classic Queen of the Skies, flown with a flight engineer and a round-dial cockpit. The 747-200F's nose door takes outsized freight just like its younger sibling. PAC flies it on heavy-lift charters and long-haul lanes where crews want the full three-person, steam-gauge experience.
B742F.main_deck: 29 main-deck pallet positions, nose and side cargo doors

B748F.description: The flagship of the fleet. The 747-8F's hinged nose door lets PAC load outsized single pieces straight through the front of the aircraft: transformers, aircraft engines, oil equipment. It carries the most of any aircraft in the fleet and anchors the transpacific and Asia to Europe network.
B748F.main_deck: 34 main-deck pallet positions, nose and side cargo doors

B744F.description: The Boeing 747-400F (Freighter) is an all-cargo, wide-body commercial airliner derived from the iconic 747-400 passenger series. Renowned as the "Queen of the Skies," this high-capacity heavy freighter features a distinctive main deck nose-loading door alongside a large side cargo door, enabling the seamless transport of oversized freight and up to 30 standard main deck pallets. Optimized for intercontinental logistics, it combines long-range capability, structural reliability, and massive payload capacity to serve as the backbone of global virtual airline cargo networks.
B744F.name: Boeing 747-400F
